prd_items.note: Statement keeps connect(address, connectTimeout) then createSocket(plain, host, port, true); AC-4 forbids self-connecting createSocket; AC-3 observes the host for every https target.
Implementation turns host name verification on; wrong-host backend gives 502 CONNECT_FAILED also with a private-CA factory.

Statement names setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("HTTPS") and HttpsURLConnection.getDefaultHostnameVerifier() fallback; AC-6 tests the fallback with an injected verifier. Defect fill confirmed by probe: OpenJDK 17.0.20 HttpsURLConnection$DefaultHostnameVerifier.verify returns false for localhost and example.com.

Every AC-A13 clause is present (no Content-Type, Content-Length: 5 and 5 bytes, HEAD/304 bodyless, 204 neither, -1 unknown length, -2 IAE, 3-byte stream aborts, no Cache-Control under defaultCache); the 304 Content-Length clause is narrowed per user decision U-2/PRD-271, not weakened unilaterally.

AC-B29 values present: three backends 502 CONNECT_FAILED, one TCP connection each under .retries(2), private CA reaches first backend, wrong host still 502, SNI = target host. SNI oracle uses a dotted host; the defect fill is confirmed by probe (OpenJDK 17.0.20: ClientHello for createSocket(plain,"localhost",...) does not contain the name, for "backend.test" it does).

Core commits the length to the adapter on 304; in-memory adapter delivers it; TinyHttpd 3.1.1 omits it (verified: ExchangeResponse.commit at e73cd5d sets no lengthHeader for status 304; managed() swallows the Content-Length header); servlet adapter hands it to the container. TinyHttpd unchanged (FR-ENGINE-014 notes: do not work around it). Note: embedded Jetty 9.4.58 does write Content-Length: 5 on a 304 (probe), so FR-SVL-010 AC-4's either-way acceptance is looser than needed but not contrary to PRD-271.

srs_items.note: Statement matches request §3.9 https bullet; adds TOTAL_TIMEOUT under watchdog (fills D-063).
AC-B29 first sentence verbatim in substance.

srs_items.note: Consistent with AC-B20 (handshake timeout with connectTimeout 1 s is CONNECT_TIMEOUT) and Implementation Notes ordering (watchdog deadline checked first).

srs_items.note: Defect verified by probe. Referencing javax/net/ssl/HttpsURLConnection does not put java/net/HttpURLConnection in the constant pool (javap), so no clash with FR-PROXY-020 AC-3.
Chooses the reflection branch of PRD-164.
IR-PROXY-001 AC-3 pins sslSocketFactory(javax.net.ssl.SSLSocketFactory) as the only TLS option.
Statement not amended for the 304 exception; see finding internal-coherence-7-1.
TinyHttpd commit adds only Date, Server, app headers, Content-Length/TE, Connection; no default Content-Type.
Verified against TinyHttpd e73cd5d (v3.1.1) ExchangeResponse.commit: 304 -> discard, lengthHeader -1; HEAD -> lengthHeader = contentLength; 204 -> none. RFC 9110 §8.6 permits CL on 304 (MAY).
Implementation Notes line refs verified (snapshotHeaders :166, onAbort :341-342, abort :355); notes agree with AC-4.
Servlet part of AC-A1 (JSON and gzip).
Testable: handed-over value read on the HttpServletResponse; client CL either 5 or absent. Probe: Jetty 9.4.58 writes Content-Length: 5 on a 304 (with and without flush) and on HEAD.

evidence.detail: docs/spec/06.engine-adapter.srs.md:2034 (FR-ENGINE-014 statement): "put `res.relay` responses on the wire with exactly the `Content-Type` the app set, the `Content-Length` taken from the length argument, the bodyless `HEAD`, `204` and `304` rules of FR-HTTP-037" — and FR-HTTP-037's rule (docs/spec/04.http-core.srs.md:5482) is "keeping a non-negative length as `Content-Length` for `HEAD` and `304`"; versus docs/spec/06.engine-adapter.srs.md:2047 (FR-ENGINE-014 AC-5): "answers a `304` response with no body bytes and no `Content-Length`".

findings.description: The amendment changed AC-5 and the notes but not the statement: the statement still says the TinyHttpd wire carries the Content-Length taken from the length argument under FR-HTTP-037's rule that keeps it on 304, while AC-5 says TinyHttpd sends none on 304.

evidence.detail: PRD-271 "(서블릿·인메모리 어댑터는 전달 ...)" vs FR-SVL-010 AC-4 "the client seeing `Content-Length: 5` only if the container writes it for a 304". Not contradicting: the adapter does hand it over ("전달"), and on the embedded Jetty 9.4.58 the client does receive Content-Length: 5 (probe in scratchpad jetty/JettyProbe.java).

findings.description: Possible weakening of PRD-271 for the servlet adapter; dropped because the adapter's part is stated and observed. Optional tightening: on embedded Jetty the test could require Content-Length: 5.

evidence.detail: Statement "so that SNI carries the target host name" vs AC-3 "the JDK sends no SNI for the dotless name `localhost`". The statement's clause is a purpose of the createSocket(plain, host, ...) call, which AC-3 requires for every target; the dated Rationale bullet records the platform limit.

Checked: javac --release 8 of a call to HttpsURLConnection.getDefaultHostnameVerifier() gives constant-pool entries only for javax/net/ssl/HttpsURLConnection (javap -v), not java/net/HttpURLConnection.

findings.description: SEC-PROXY-005 fallback verifier does not break FR-PROXY-020 AC-3's class-reference ban.

evidence.detail: FR-HTTP-037 statement "keeping a non-negative length as `Content-Length` for `HEAD` and `304`" is scoped by its AC-5 ("commits `Content-Length: 5` ... to the adapter ... whether a client receives the `Content-Length` of a `304` is the adapter's choice") and AC-9 ("in the headers it commits to the adapter").

findings.description: Core requirement does not contradict FR-ENGINE-014 AC-5 or FR-SVL-010 AC-4; FR-PROXY-014 AC-5 and OPS-DX-009 AC-7 use the same adapter-dependent wording.

evidence.detail: OPS-DX-009 AC-4 "keeps a non-negative length as `Content-Length` without a body for HEAD and 304" and AC-7 "the client sees that `Content-Length` only where the adapter writes it: TinyHttpd 3.1.1 omits it" describe relay's commit and the adapter's wire result respectively; both can be documented together.

findings.description: No contradiction with FR-ENGINE-014 AC-5 / FR-SVL-010 AC-4 (HEAD keeps CL on every built-in adapter in all three).
